- To update by hand, download the new installer from the same address and run it. The wizard closes the running app, replaces the files and starts it again. The **Start seowatcher when Windows starts** (Turkish: "Windows açılınca seowatcher'ı başlat") checkbox in the wizard shows your current setting from the menu.

Your data, your Google connection and your settings stay as they are. An automatic update does not touch the **Windows açılınca başlat** (Start with Windows) setting.

### Company deployment

For IT teams that want to install for all users of a computer, or install silently with a deployment tool (Intune, GPO, PDQ):

- **For all users**: run the installer as administrator and choose the "all users" option in the wizard. The app installs under `C:\Program Files\seowatcher` (the per-user install goes to `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\seowatcher`). Each user's data still stays in their own `%LOCALAPPDATA%\seowatcher` folder.
- **Silent install**: `seowatcher-setup.exe /VERYSILENT /NORESTART` (single user) or `seowatcher-setup.exe /VERYSILENT /ALLUSERS /NORESTART` (administrator, all users). When a silent install finishes, the app opens by itself.
- **Install log**: every install writes to `%LOCALAPPDATA%\seowatcher\logs\setup.log`. You can give another place with `/LOG="path"`.
- **Silent uninstall**: `unins000.exe /VERYSILENT` (in the install folder: `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\seowatcher` for a per-user install, `C:\Program Files\seowatcher` for all users).
- **Verification**: before each version is published, it is installed on a clean Windows machine, opened, left running until the health address responds, and uninstalled. A version is not published until this test passes.

### Repair

If something gets stuck, right-click the icon and click **Kurulumu onar** (Repair installation); if the icon is not visible, click the ^ arrow on the taskbar. The app clears temporary files and checks that the package is complete. When it then opens, it runs the database update again.

If a file has been deleted from the package (for example, an antivirus program quarantined it), the app downloads the installer of the installed version from GitHub, verifies its fingerprint and reinstalls itself. Your data is not touched. If there is no internet connection, it says "Kurulum eksik" (Installation incomplete) and opens the releases page; then download the installer and run it.

### Uninstall

1. In Windows, open **Settings → Apps → Installed apps** and find **seowatcher**.
2. Click **Uninstall**.

The uninstaller removes the program, the Start menu shortcut the "start with Windows" entry (including one you turned on from the menu) and downloaded update files. It does not touch the data folder, and the uninstall window says so too. If you also want to delete your database, your Google connection and your reports, delete the data folder yourself.

### Where is the data and how do I back it up?

Everything is in one folder: `%LOCALAPPDATA%\seowatcher`. Type this into the File Explorer address bar. The **Veri klasörünü aç** (Open data folder) menu item goes there too. It holds:

- `data`: the database (projects, the Search Console archive, audits, reports).
- `instance-secret`: the key that encrypts the Google access keys. If it is lost, you must set up the Google connections again from scratch.
- `mcp-token`: the password your AI assistant uses when it connects to the app.
- `server.env`, `config.json`, `logs`.

To make a backup:

1. Close the app with **Çıkış** (Exit).
2. Copy the whole folder.

To restore, close the app, put the folder back in place and start the app. Moving to another computer works the same way. If you take the `instance-secret` file too, the Google connections keep working.

### Changing the port number

The app uses port 3001. If another program holds it, the app picks the first free number from 3002 to 3010, but only for that one start, and shows a "3001 numarası dolu, 3002 kullanılıyor" (Port 3001 is in use, using 3002) balloon. It does not save this number. When 3001 is free again, the app uses 3001 on the next start, because the redirect addresses at Google contain this number.

To choose a specific port:

1. Close the app.
2. Open the `config.json` file in the data folder with Notepad.
3. Write this in it:

```json
{
  "port": 3005
}
```

4. Save it and start the app. If the file has other lines (such as `autoUpdate`), do not delete them; change only the value of `port`.

When the number changes, also update the two redirect addresses at Google with the new number. These addresses are explained in the Google connection guide.

## Check

- When you hover over the taskbar icon (if it is not visible, click the ^ arrow on the taskbar), it should read "seowatcher X.Y.Z: Çalışıyor: http://127.0.0.1:3001/" (seowatcher 0.5.0 Alpha: Running: http://127.0.0.1:3001/). The version number is the one you installed.
- In the browser, the address `http://127.0.0.1:3001/api/health` should show a text that starts with "status":"ok".
- On the **Help** screen, the "Your setup status" card should say "Everything looks good.". Before Google is connected, the "Google sign-in" row asks for attention. This is normal.

## Frequently asked questions

**Why does it open in the browser?** The app runs on your computer like a small server. The browser is its screen.

**What happens when I turn off the computer?** The app closes too. If **Windows açılınca başlat** (Start with Windows) is checked, it starts by itself the next time the computer starts.

**Can I open it from another computer?** No, and this is on purpose. The app listens only on the 127.0.0.1 address. To open it to the internet, you need to put your own authentication in front of it.

**Can I switch from the Docker version?** Yes, but the data does not move by itself. You need to create the projects and connect Google again. The Search Console archive fills up again on the first launch.

**My antivirus gave a warning.** Some antivirus programs warn because the file is unsigned. Download the file only from the GitHub releases page and compare its SHA-256 hash.

## If something goes wrong

- **The icon says "Hata: 3001 ve sonraki 9 adres numarası (port) dolu" (Error: 3001 and the next 9 ports are in use).** Another program holds these numbers. Write another number in the `config.json` file.
- **The icon says "Veritabanı güncellemesi başarısız" (Database update failed).** Click **Günlükleri aç** (Open logs) and check the last lines of `migrate.log`. Usually the disk is full or the folder is read-only.
- **The icon says "Sunucu beklenmedik şekilde kapandı" (The server closed unexpectedly) or "Sunucu 10 dakikada üç kez kapandı" (The server closed three times in 10 minutes).** The last lines of `server.log` give the reason. Try **Yeniden başlat** (Restart), and if that does not help, **Kurulumu onar** (Repair installation). If it still does not help, click **Sorunu bildir (GitHub)** (Report a problem (GitHub)).
- **The icon says "Veritabanı güncellemesi 15 dakikada bitmedi" (The database update did not finish in 15 minutes).** Another program may have locked the database file (a backup or sync program). Stop that program and click **Yeniden başlat** (Restart).
- **The browser did not open.** Double-click the icon or type the address by hand: `http://127.0.0.1:3001`



## Windows notifications

Right-click the seowatcher tray icon and use **Windows bildirimleri** (Windows notifications, on by default). While the launcher runs, completed/failed audits from all projects and new announcements appear as Windows balloons within about 90 seconds, even with the browser closed or in the background. Click to open the relevant page; several events form one summary. First use skips old events; restarting does not replay seen events. Events received while muted are not replayed later. New-version notifications follow the existing update setting. Windows Focus/Do not disturb can hide notifications. No notifications appear when the launcher is closed. This feature is unavailable in Docker.

---

# Installing with Docker

URL: https://seowatcher.io/en/docs/install-docker/

> Install with Docker on Mac, Linux and Windows. One command is enough, and no .env file is needed. Your data stays in Docker's data volume.

This guide gets the app running in Docker (a program that runs apps in isolated containers) at `http://localhost:3001`. If you use Windows, the single-file Windows installation is much easier; this guide is for Mac, Linux and people who already use Docker. The first start takes a few minutes because the app is built inside the container. Later starts take seconds.

## What you need

- Docker Desktop (Mac, Windows) or Docker Engine with Docker Compose (Linux).
- On Windows, Docker Desktop also needs WSL 2 and virtualization enabled in the BIOS/UEFI.
- Git. If you do not have it, **Code → Download ZIP** on the GitHub page also works.
- About 2 GB of free disk space, and 2 GB of free memory during the first build.

## Steps

1. Download the repository (the project files) and go into its folder:

```sh
git clone https://github.com/ucsahinn/seotracker.git
cd seotracker
```

2. Start the app:

```sh
docker compose up -d
```

That is all. No `.env` file is needed. The encryption key and the assistant password are created automatically on first start and stored in Docker's data volume.

3. To follow the progress, run:

```sh
docker compose logs -f
```

4. Wait. The log line "Building client + server" marks the first build. Wait until `docker compose ps` shows the status **healthy**, then open `http://localhost:3001` in the browser.

The next step is the Google connection guide. On Docker, the two redirect addresses you enter at Google are:

- `http://localhost:3001/api/gsc/oauth/callback`
- `http://localhost:3001/api/ga4/oauth/callback`

### Updating

Run these two commands:

```sh
git pull
docker compose up -d --build
```

**Settings → About** tells you about the new version and shows these two commands. Your data stays in the data volume named `seotracker_data`, so updating does not delete it.

### Stopping and removing

- To stop: `docker compose stop`
- To start again: `docker compose up -d`
- To remove the container and keep the data: `docker compose down`
- To delete the data too: `docker compose down -v`. This command permanently deletes the database, the Google connections and the reports.

### Backing up

Your data is in the `seotracker_data` volume, at the path `/app/.wrangler` inside the container. To make a backup, run these three commands in order:

```sh
docker compose stop
docker run --rm -v seotracker_data:/data -v "$PWD":/backup alpine tar czf /backup/seotracker-yedek.tgz -C /data .
docker compose up -d
```

To restore, use `tar xzf` instead of `tar czf` in the same command. The `instance-secret` file in the data volume is the key that encrypts the Google connections. A backup that lacks it restores without the Google connections.

### Settings (optional)

No setting is required. To change something, put a `.env` file in the project folder and then run `docker compose up -d --force-recreate seotracker`.

| Setting name                           | What it does                                                                                                                                 |
| -------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| PORT                                   | The port number, 3001 by default. When it changes, the Google redirect addresses change too                                                  |
| ALLOWED_HOST                           | The public host name, if the app runs behind another server. If empty, only localhost                                                        |
| AUTH_MODE                              | `local_noauth` (default) or `cloudflare_access`                                                                                              |
| BETTER_AUTH_SECRET                     | The encryption key. Leave it empty and the app creates one. If you set it by hand, use at least 32 characters and never change it afterwards |
| GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID, GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET | An alternative to entering them on the **Settings** screen. A value entered on the screen takes priority                                     |
| PAGESPEED_API_KEY                      | An alternative to entering it on the **Settings** screen                                                                                     |
| MCP_TOKEN                              | If empty, it is created on first start. If you write `off`, no password is asked. Any other value is used as it is                           |

## Check

- In the output of `docker compose ps`, the status should be **healthy**. On the first start, it can take up to five minutes to get there.
- The output of `curl.exe http://127.0.0.1:3001/api/health` should start with "status":"ok". You can also open `http://127.0.0.1:3001/api/health` in the browser.
- `http://localhost:3001` should open in the browser. The status card on the **Help** screen should say "Everything looks good." Before you connect Google, the "Google sign-in" row asks for attention. This is normal.

## Frequently asked questions

**Why is the first start long?** The app is built inside the container. On later starts, the build is skipped.

**Where is the `.env.example` file?** There is none. That file, inherited from the upstream project, described things that are not in this version. The full list is in the table above and in the `docs/ENVIRONMENT.md` file.

**Can I open it to the internet?** The app does not ask who you are, so do not open it to the internet without your own authentication in front of it. If you set `ALLOWED_HOST`, the app warns you in the health check.

**Where do I get my assistant's password?** The **Agent setup** screen in the app shows the command: `docker compose exec -T seotracker cat /app/.wrangler/mcp-token`. If you use Git Bash, put `MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1` in front of the command.

## If something goes wrong

- **It says "Bind for 127.0.0.1:3001 failed".** The port number is in use. Put a `.env` file with the line `PORT=3002` in the project folder and recreate the container. On Windows, Notepad may save the file as `.env.txt`; in PowerShell, `Set-Content -Encoding ascii .env 'PORT=3002'` avoids that.
- **The status is "unhealthy".** `docker compose logs --tail 50` shows the last lines. If memory ran out during the build, give Docker Desktop more memory.
- **The Google connection says it "isn't configured".** If `BETTER_AUTH_SECRET` is shorter than 32 characters, Google stays off. If you set it by hand, make it longer. If you did not, the `instance-secret` file in the data volume may be damaged.
- **The Google connection dropped after an update.** `BETTER_AUTH_SECRET` changed, or the data volume was recreated. Choose **Reconnect** in the project settings.

---

# Connecting to Google

URL: https://seowatcher.io/en/docs/google-connection/

> Connect Search Console and GA4 with your own Google Cloud service account or OAuth client, then choose the properties for each project.

seowatcher reads Search Console and Google Analytics 4 with your own Google Cloud credential: a service account or an OAuth client. You save the credential once for the whole installation, then choose a Search Console property and a GA4 property for each project.

## Credentials and properties have different scopes

Google credentials in Settings apply to the installation. The property in Project settings → Connections belongs to one project. Stored means the credential was saved; Property selected means the binding was saved. Neither verifies report access. Check the latest source state in Search performance or Analytics. Analytics shows the property timezone and currency beside its identity. Selecting a property does not install website tracking.

## Service account

Enable Search Console API and, for Analytics, Admin API and Data API in Google Cloud. Create a service account and download its JSON key. In Settings → Service account, select the file or use the masked paste field, then save. The private key is not displayed. Add the visible account email to Search Console with Full access and Analytics with Viewer access. Then choose each project's property.

## OAuth alternative

Create a Google Cloud OAuth Web application client. Register both callback URLs shown in Settings exactly. Save the client ID and secret in Settings. Authorize Google from project connections and choose the property. A stored service account takes priority over OAuth.

## Recovery

A failed list refresh preserves the previous properties. An empty list alone does not prove missing access. Reconnect expired grants; check property permissions for denied access and the Cloud project for disabled APIs. Wait and retry rate limits. For unknown failures use Retry and Help diagnostics. Removing a credential here does not revoke it at Google. Changing a project domain preserves its property binding and history.

The connection card dates the last already-observed Google read for the current credential and property; after a temporary failure it retains the previous successful read's date. Without history, access remains unverified. Opening settings makes no Google query. Credential changes do not transfer old access or quota evidence to the new identity; explicitly refresh reports.

---

# PageSpeed key

URL: https://seowatcher.io/en/docs/pagespeed-key/

> Save your PageSpeed Insights API key, check test requests and understand request quotas and the counters shown during site audits.

A PageSpeed Insights API key lets the site audit measure the speed of your pages with Google's PageSpeed Insights. You create the key for free in Google Cloud, and it is optional: without one, the app tries to measure at most 50 pages per audit.

## Add a key

Enable PageSpeed Insights API in Google Cloud. Create an API key and restrict it to PageSpeed Insights. Save it in Settings → Speed measurement. The key is encrypted and never displayed. Docker can also use PAGESPEED_API_KEY; the Settings value takes priority.

## What the test proves

Test key makes one real mobile request for example.com. It does not measure your site or increment the audit measurement counter. A result and test date appear. The button remains disabled while pending and for at least ten seconds from the click. Changing the key removes the old test result.

## Limits and recovery

Without a key, the application attempts at most 50 pages per audit. Google may stop requests earlier; a key does not guarantee success. Check actual quota in Google Cloud. The Settings PageSpeed counter includes only audits started within the last 24 hours, excluding key tests and other programs.

For an invalid key, copy it again. For 403/restricted, check API activation and key restrictions. Wait for rate or daily quota limits and inspect the Cloud quota screen. Retry network failures. A stored key is configuration evidence; a successful test proves only that request succeeded.

---

# Projects

URL: https://seowatcher.io/en/docs/projects/

> Projects helps you choose a site and complete its missing connections. Each project keeps its own Google properties, audits and reports.

Projects helps you choose a site and complete its missing connections. Each project keeps its own Google properties, audits and reports.

## Read the screen

With multiple projects, search by name or domain and sort by either. **Last opened** is the project remembered by this browser, not an SEO status. Continue with **Add site**, **Connect Search Console**, or **Open dashboard**, according to the known configuration. **Project context** opens notes; **Settings** opens configuration.

**Search archive** means locally stored Web search data for all devices and countries. The dates are visible. The window ends on the newest stored day, which may be old. With missing days, clicks are the subtotal of observed days only. A missing day is a gap, not zero. A change is shown only when both periods are complete. Equal totals say “Unchanged”; changes from zero include explicit previous and current counts. Archive details show the last stored day and available read timestamp. Legacy records do not identify the evidence used to establish finality.

The audit belongs to the selected site's own host. The last completed snapshot and a newer failed or running attempt are distinct. A stored connection does not prove a successful Google read. Unavailable sources are neither disconnected nor measured zero: use **Retry**. Refresh reads identities and local facts together; it does not call Google or start an audit.

## Create and manage

Choose **New project**, enter a name, optional domain, country and language. Creating it collects no data. Choose Google properties in **Settings → Connections**. General settings change identity and market. One project has one Search Console and one Analytics property.

Archiving preserves data. **Archived → Restore** brings the project back. The last remaining project cannot be archived. Search clicks differ from GA4 sessions and query-archive totals. Projects with different dates are not added together.

When the previous period has fewer than 20 clicks, the badge shows the click difference instead of a percentage. For example, 1 to 5 is +4 clicks; with small counts, that change alone is not strong evidence of growth.

---

# Dashboard

URL: https://seowatcher.io/en/docs/dashboard/

> The Dashboard brings together search traffic, measured next tasks and source limitations.

The Dashboard brings together search traffic, measured next tasks and source limitations. Refresh rereads the active Dashboard sources, setup state and Google configuration. If a read fails, it reports a partial refresh. The data retrieval time is separate from the latest measured day.

## Search summary

The default scope is 28 days of Web search across all devices and countries. Unfinished recent days are excluded. The visible dates and Pacific time zone define the window. Source lines show the actual previous dates, latest data day and excluded days. If Google supplies no completeness date, the assumed exclusion is disclosed. Hidden queries and row limits mean query lists are not complete site totals.

Clicks count visits from Google search results; impressions count appearances in results. CTR divides clicks by impressions. Average position is impression-weighted; lower is better. All four tiles open Search performance with the same default scope. Growth from a zero baseline uses an absolute count; a fall to zero can show a valid negative percentage. A missing previous period produces no invented change. The faded daily-click line shows the previous period.

## Next tasks and setup

Up to three tasks come from connection problems, measured audit findings, actual search tasks or an old crawl. Being connected alone does not generate an opportunity. A failed audit read never becomes first-use advice. No priority task within measured scope does not certify every source as healthy.

Setup uses the same six signals as Project context. Missing and unreadable signals are separate. An own-site completed audit becomes stale at exactly seven days. Setup preferences is a collapsed optional tour, without another readiness score. Deferred steps remain restorable when no active steps remain.

## Query estimates

Eligible queries have enough impressions and a rounded average position of 4–20. Extra clicks model movement to the next position band and are an upper bound, not measured traffic. Known and unknown estimates are counted over the whole eligible set before the top four rows are shown. All-unknown never becomes a zero bound. Confirmed, suggested and absent brand separation are disclosed. Do not add this query estimate to the page-based Opportunities total, which has a different unit and period basis.

## Own-site audit

Only crawls matching the project domain are selected. A newer crawl of another site is ignored. The last completed snapshot and a newer running or failed attempt are identified separately. Without a domain, the Dashboard links to project settings. The card names the start address, date, measured checks and any page cap.

Unique affected pages, failed check types and severity page–type pairs are different units. One page can fail three checks. Information notes sit outside the critical/warning bar. Health wording applies only to measured scope. Missing measurements or a page cap cannot certify the entire site. Comparisons require matching start scope, settings, crawled URL sets and usable measurements. Only checks measured in both crawls produce changes; a narrower or unreadable crawl cannot count as a fix. Unknown scope is explained. Worst-page links open the same audit’s issues focused on the selected URL.

## Analytics outcomes

Organic sessions, active users, engagement and key events come from Google Analytics. Actual dates and the property time zone are visible. Sessions differ from Google clicks and include other organic search engines. Unknown or restricted sessions never mean zero traffic; other readable metrics remain visible. Privacy thresholds, sampling and access restrictions are disclosed. Unreliable comparisons are withheld and missing limited daily values remain gaps.

Positive commerce evidence in either period keeps revenue and orders visible, including a measured quiet zero period. With no such evidence, sales measurement is described as unverified. Unknown currency is explicitly labelled.

## Limits

The Dashboard has no keyword volume, backlink or competitor-ranking data. Every result depends on its source window and coverage. Reconcile real Google data using identical dates and filters.

## Interpreting small samples

When the comparison period has fewer clicks than the analysis threshold, the summary leads with actual clicks and impressions. Percentages and averages alone do not establish growth or loss with little data. An empty opportunity list does not mean no query ranks at 4–20: the period-scaled impression threshold and brand exclusion also apply.

The audit identifier stays in navigation; the card shows the starting URL. Unknown sessions call for checking source warnings in the Analytics report, connection access and the site tag. The sales measurement note is inside the Organic revenue disclosure.

---

# Search performance

URL: https://seowatcher.io/en/docs/search-performance/

> See how often you show up on Google, how many clicks you get and what to fix first. The numbers come from Search Console. Gain figures are an upper bound.

Here you see how often you show up on Google, how many clicks you get and what to fix first.

Clicks, impressions, CTR and position come straight from Search Console. The app does not estimate any of them. Estimates appear only in the "possible gain" figures, and those are always marked as an "upper bound".

The filters you choose are written into the address bar. If you like, share that view as a link or bookmark it.

## Three terms

**Final day.** Search Console keeps counting a day for several days. Totals and comparisons use only days whose count has finished. Days follow the Pacific time Google uses. Days that are still being counted show hatched on the chart and are left out of the totals.

**Hidden query.** Google does not list very rarely searched queries, for privacy. But it adds their clicks to the site total. That is why the query table adds up to less than the site total. The difference is the hidden queries.

**Upper bound.** A gain figure means "at most this much". It is the extra clicks a search would get if it rose one step, at your own site's click-through rates. The real result depends on competitors and on Google, and is usually smaller.

## What is on the screen

**Top bar.** Four things sit at the top right.

- **Refresh**: asks Search Console for fresh data. The app normally reuses an answer from a few minutes ago.
- **Download report**: turns the view on screen into a printable one-file report, saves it and downloads it. The report also sits in the **Reports** screen.
- The export menu: **Queries (CSV)**, **Pages (CSV)**, **Queries close to the top three (CSV)**, **Export queries to Sheets**, **Export pages to Sheets**. Exports follow the filters on screen. If you have a search or a quick filter on the Queries or Pages tab, it carries into the file too.

**Filters.** A one-line bar summarises the chosen filters: "(Web, All devices, All countries, Last 28 days, Against previous period)". Open it to see: **Search type** (Web, Image, Video, News), **Device filter** (All devices, Mobile, Desktop, Tablet), **Country filter** (the countries Google reports for that period), **Date range** (Last 7 days, Last 28 days, Last 3 months) and **Comparison** (Against previous period, Against last year, No comparison).

**Data status.** A strip that says what the numbers rest on. For example "Data is final up to 24 Oct; the last 3 days are still being counted (hatched on the chart)." The same strip shows which days the comparison uses and the name of your Search Console property. Press the property name to go to the project's connection settings. If last year's comparison is chosen and Google no longer gives those days, the strip says so (Google goes back 16 months at most). Open **About the data** to see: the date of the final days, how many days are still being counted and the last data date, the share of clicks from hidden queries, whether the tables were read in full (Google returns a limited number of rows at a time) and whether this view sent new requests to Google or used an answer taken a few minutes ago.

**Summary sentence.** A sentence or two above the tiles says what happened. For example "Clicks rose 6.1% in the last 28 days against the previous period. CTR fell 0.3 points." Then it says how many extra clicks the first three jobs could bring together, marked "(upper bound)". The **To do** link takes you to that tab.

**Four tiles.** **Clicks**, **Impressions**, **CTR** (what percentage of impressions were clicked) and **Average position**. All are totals of the final days. Each tile shows the change against the comparison you chose, and a small line. The change in clicks and impressions is written as a percentage, in CTR as points and in position as places. For average position, a small number is good, and 1 is the top spot. The direction of a change is shown with an arrow as well as colour.

**Over time chart.** It draws the daily values.

- The picker at the top right switches between four measures: clicks, impressions, CTR and average position. On the position chart, up is a better position.
- The **Day**, **Week** and **Month** buttons change the time unit. The comparison line (a dashed line) appears only in the day view.
- The hatched area is days Google is still counting. A hollow dot means an incomplete or not yet final period.
- Numbered markers above the line show three things: ranking updates Google announced ("Google update"), the days site audits finished ("Site audit completed") and your own notes. Under the chart, each number is explained.
- **Add a note** leaves your own note on a date, for example "New page titles went live". A note is at most 280 characters. It helps you remember later why something dropped or rose. Notes outside the chosen period are collected under "Notes outside this period (N)".

**Start with these strip.** Between the chart and the tabs, the first three to-dos sit side by side. Each has its title, its possible gain and a button. **All to-dos (N)** takes you to the To do tab.

**Tabs.** There are seven: **To do (N)**, **Queries (N)**, **Pages (N)**, **Ranking opportunities (N)**, **Changes**, **Overlaps** and **Distribution**. The number in brackets is the count of rows or findings inside the tab. If queries or pages are falling, the Changes tab reads "Changes (N falling)". When you switch tabs, the search box and the quick filter reset.

### To do

The app ranks the jobs it finds in Search Console data by estimated gain. Jobs are grouped by kind, and each group's heading says how many jobs it holds:

- "N queries close to the top three": searches with an average position between 4 and 20 and enough impressions. Brand searches are left out of this list. Strengthen the page for that search.
- "N results get few clicks for their position": searches clicked less than your site's other searches at the same position. Rewrite the title and description.
- "Clicks fell for N queries" and "Clicks fell for N pages": a clear drop against the previous period. If the position fell too, update the content. If the position held, review the title and description.
- "N pages are losing their old strength": pages that fell far below the best of the previous four quarters in the last quarter. Refresh the page.
- "N pages are seen but never clicked". The gain estimate here is cautious: it uses the click-through rate of the position band below the page's own, not its own band. Pages on page two or further back get no estimate.
- "You no longer appear for N queries": searches that got clicks in the previous period and no impressions now.
- "You trail on N device types" and "You trail in N countries".
- "Unusual drops on N days": that day's clicks or impressions were unusually low against the same weekday in earlier weeks.
- "Set your brand name": appears when no brand name is set, so brand searches can be separated. When the app is splitting them with names it suggested from your domain, the job reads "Confirm your brand name" instead. Confirm the suggestions if they are right, or enter your brand's name.

In each group's heading, **Why, and what to do** gives the reason and what to do. A row shows its rank number, the finding, the evidence (for example "Position 8.2 · 640 impressions · 12 clicks"), the possible gain written as "≈ +N clicks" and a confidence label (**Confidence: high**, medium or low). The first four jobs of a group are shown, and **Show all (N)** opens the rest.

You mark a job with **Done**. Marked jobs go under "Marked as done (N)" and come back with **Restore**. The done marks are kept only in this browser. **Details** (or **Open this breakdown**) on a row opens the detail of that search, page, device or country. If there are several jobs for one search or page, the total at the top counts it once.

### Queries and Pages

A table by searches or by pages. The columns are **Query** (or **Page**), **Clicks**, **Click change** (against the comparison), **Impressions**, **CTR** and **Position**. Click a heading to sort. The bar behind a row is its share of the clicks in this table. The box at the top searches among the rows. Beside it, "{shown} / {total} rows" is written.

**Quick filters.** For queries: **In the top 10**, **Position 4-10**, **Position 11-20**, **Low CTR**, **No clicks**. For pages: **In the top 10**, **Clicked**, **Low CTR**, **No clicks**. Low CTR means a row on page one with at least 100 impressions and a click-through below 2 percent.

**Row menu.** In the three dots: **Open page in a new tab**, **Copy URL**, **Copy keyword**, **Save as keyword**. What you save goes to the **Saved keywords** screen. Clicking a row opens the detail panel.

The note under the table gives the base: "read N queries, N clicks. The site total is N clicks; the difference comes from the queries Google hides." If Google's row limit was reached, the least-clicked end is missing from the list and the note says so.

### Ranking opportunities

There are four sections.

- **Queries close to the top three.** Searches with an average position between 4 and 20. Brand searches are not included. It says how many extra clicks they could bring together if each rose one step (from 6-10 to 4-5, from 4-5 to 2-3, from 11-20 to page one). That is an upper bound. The total covers every query in this range, not only the rows listed, and is followed by the dates it covers, for example "Period: Sep 27, 2026 – Oct 24, 2026." When only the largest gains are listed, a note below says "The N with the largest gain are listed." The table shows **Query**, **Target page**, **Position**, **Impressions**, **Clicks** and **Possible gain**. The target page is the page Google shows most for that search. You take the searches you select with **Copy keywords** or **Save as keyword**.
- **Results clicked less than their position suggests.** Searches whose click-through falls below 70 percent of your site's rate for results at the same position. The gain comes without any change in position, only by rewriting the title and description. The table shows the search's rate, the rate **Expected at this position** and the possible gain.
- **Pages that show up but never get clicked.** Pages that got at least 100 impressions (for 28 days) in the period and not one click.
- **Your site's CTR by position.** The yardstick for the gains above. It is the click-through rate of your own results at each position, not other sites'. If a position has too few searches or impressions, it says "Not enough data" and no estimate is made for it. If you defined brand names, these rates are calculated from non-brand searches.

### Changes

It compares the chosen period with the previous one.

- **Biggest changes since the previous period.** Two lists: **Falling (N)** and **Rising (N)**. For a search or page to enter a list, its clicks must move by at least 3 clicks and 20 percent of its previous value. Small moves do not enter. A row shows the previous and new clicks, impressions and position.
- **Newly showing** and **Lost (with their previous-period numbers).** Only searches that got at least 50 impressions (for 28 days) in just one period. If one period's table is incomplete because of the row limit, it cannot be known which search is new or lost, and the screen says so.
- **Pages losing ground.** Pages whose clicks in the last quarter (91 days) fell below 70 percent of the best of the previous four quarters, and are also behind the same quarter last year. This comparison needs more than a year of data. If Search Console did not give data that old, or a filter is on, the screen says so.
- **Long term: monthly clicks.** Search Console goes back 16 months. The app keeps the daily totals longer on this computer. The bars show monthly clicks. A bar with a dashed outline is a month the archive does not hold in full. If the archive is still filling, the screen says "No days in the archive yet" or gives the start date. This section follows the device filter, not the country filter.

### Overlaps

It shows cases where several of your pages appear for the same search. Pages can split each other's clicks. Most of the time it is enough to make one the main page and link to it from the others. The card's heading reads "Pages competing for one query".

- Three tiles: **Queries with competing pages**, **Impressions going to the other pages** and **Query losing the most**. Press the last tile and the list narrows to that query.
- The **Pages competing for the same query** table shows, for each query, its pages, their clicks, impressions and positions. The page Google shows most for that query counts as the "preferred" one. The share of impressions going to the others is written as "outside the share".
- This analysis looks at 28 days. If 7 days is chosen, it is raised to 28 for the analysis and the real date range is written. Only searches with at least 100 impressions are examined. For a page to join the contest, it needs at least 10 impressions and a 20 percent share on that search.
- If the search hits Search Console's row limit, the screen warns that some queries could not be examined.

### Distribution

- **Position distribution.** Shows in groups which positions your searches appear at. If the archive holds at least two weeks, **Queries by week** appears below it. This chart covers Web searches only. With Image, Video or News selected as the search type, it says "The weekly distribution is for Web searches only." in its place. That chart shows the share of the position groups week by week. It comes from the query archive on your computer. It is not shown with a device or country filter, because the archive does not keep those breakdowns.
- **Brand and non-brand searches.** Searches that arrive with your name and searches by people who did not know you are measured separately: **Brand searches** and **Non-brand searches**. For each, the number of queries, clicks, CTR and average position are written. If no brand name is defined, it says "Brand searches are not separated" and an **Add brand name** button appears. If the app suggested brand names from your domain, it says "Not confirmed." The measurement was then made with the suggested names. Press **Confirm suggestions** or use **Edit brand names**. Shares are of the queries read; hidden queries are not included.
- **Devices** and **Countries.** Click a device or country and the whole screen narrows to it.
- **Search appearance.** Which special formats your results show in on Google (rich results, video and so on). A rich result is a result that shows extra information such as a product or video. Google adds up this breakdown by page. If Google reported no special format, the screen says so.
- **Question searches.** Searches shaped as questions and searches of four or more words. They are the clearest source of content ideas.

**Brand names.** You enter brand names with **Edit brand names**. Enter your site's name and the ways people spell it, for example the name and its short form. Searches containing these words count as brand searches. There are **Save** and **Cancel** buttons, and the **Suggestions:** line adds a name in one click. Defining brand names changes not only this screen but also the gain estimate on the **Opportunities** screen, because that estimate leaves brand searches out.

**Detail panel.** Click a search or a page (in a table, in To do, in Ranking opportunities or in Changes) and it opens from the right. At the top it says the date range and "final days". Then come four numbers (Clicks, Impressions, CTR, Average position) and their change against the chosen comparison. Below is the **Daily clicks** line. For a page, a list "This page's queries (N)" appears; for a search, "Pages showing for this query (N)". Each row gives clicks and position. If no search is listed for a page, its clicks may come from queries Google hides. The queries may add up to less than the page's total, because hidden queries are not listed. **Open page** opens the page in a new tab. **Save as keyword** adds the search to **Saved keywords**.

## How to use it

1. First read the summary sentence at the top. It says whether clicks are rising or falling.
2. Look at the **Start with these** strip or the **To do** tab. The first three jobs are the ones that gain the most.
3. If there is a big drop, set the **Date range** to **Last 3 months**. Find the day the drop began on the chart. If a Google update or a change you made falls on that day, it shows in the markers.
4. On the **Ranking opportunities** tab, look at **Queries close to the top three**. Open the page of the three most-shown searches. Adjust the title and first paragraph to that search.
5. On the **Queries** tab, press the **Low CTR** button. Your position is good but nobody clicks. The problem is most likely the title and description.
6. On the **Changes** tab, look at **Falling**. Click the top search and read the day the drop began in the detail panel.
7. If you see pages competing for the same search on the **Overlaps** tab, first decide which page you want to answer. Then point the internal links at that page.
8. After a fix, write its date on the chart with **Add a note**. Two weeks later you see its effect on the chart.
9. When a job is finished, say **Done**. The list gets shorter.
10. At the end of the month, save the view with **Download report**.

## How the numbers are calculated

Google delivers data three days late. The range therefore ends not today but three days before. The last days can also change for a few more days. The app leaves those days out of the totals. The previous period is the period of the same length right before this range. For the last-year comparison, the same days of last year are taken. You see the change in clicks and impressions as a percentage and the change in CTR as points.

The tiles are the real totals of the site. The tables count each page that appears for the same search separately. If you add up the page table, you get a larger number than the tile. That is not an error. If you add up the query table, you get a smaller number than the tile, because hidden queries are not listed.

Google gives at most 1,000 rows at a time. If the row limit was reached, the least-clicked end is missing from the list and the screen says so.

**Possible gain.** The app applies your site's own click-through rate to each search. It takes the rate one step up from the position the search is at, multiplies it by the search's impressions and subtracts the current clicks. Searches with very few impressions do not count (at least 50 impressions for 28 days). For title problems, the yardstick is the search reaching your site's rate at the same position. Brand searches are left out. That is why every gain is an upper bound. The same calculation is used on the **Opportunities** screen.

**Confidence label.** The label beside each job shows how solid the data behind the finding is: high, medium or low.

## Frequently asked

**Why are the last three days hatched on the chart?** Google is still counting those days. They are left out of the totals. They become final in a few days.

**The table total does not match the tile.** That is normal. The tile is the site total. The query table and the page table differ because of hidden queries and because they count several pages separately.

**My position is different when I search on Google.** The position here is the average over the period. It does not reflect a single search.

**The search I look for is not in the list.** Google hides very rarely searched queries. On small sites there may be no query rows at all.

**Why did a job vanish from the To do list?** If you marked it done, it is under "Marked as done". The marks are kept only in this browser. In another browser or on another computer you see it again.

**If pages overlap, should I merge them?** Most of the time, no. First decide which page you want to answer. Then point the internal links at that page. If the pages really answer the same question, merge them.

**Do I have to enter a brand name?** No, but if you do not, people searching for your own name distort the CTR calculation and the opportunities come out incomplete. The screen reminds you with the "Set your brand name" job. When the app is using names it suggested from your domain, the job reads "Confirm your brand name".

## Limits

The Discover and Google News search types are not included. There is no search volume and no competitor position. Data does not go back further than 16 months from Google. For older data, look at the archive on this computer: the long-term chart on the **Changes** tab and the **Rank tracking** screen read from it. The done marks and notes are kept only on this installation.



Links from Opportunities and Rankings open exact URL/query details for the source dates. Overview totals remain property-wide; selected identity metrics are in the detail panel. Unreadable periods are never silently replaced. Choosing a period preset clears pinned dates. Download report sends the displayed dates to the server and is unavailable during refresh. Dates stay fixed; Google may revise the measurements read again for the report.

## Interpreting small samples

When the comparison period has fewer clicks than the analysis threshold, the summary leads with actual clicks and impressions. Percentages and averages alone do not establish growth or loss with little data. An empty opportunity list does not mean no query ranks at 4–20: the period-scaled impression threshold and brand exclusion also apply.

When the to-do list is empty, open the visible queries for review. The app does not suggest a longer period when the last three months are already selected, or assume Google will later reveal withheld queries.

---

# Ranking tracking

URL: https://seowatcher.io/en/docs/rank-tracking/

> Track average Google positions and changes for Search Console queries. Use the local archive to review records beyond Google's 16-month window.

This screen shows locally archived Search Console Web queries. Average position is not a fixed rank you will see in every search. It varies with location, device and context. Impressions are not search volume.

## Start with the supported movement

The verdict counts queries observed in both periods and movements of at least half a place. Unknown comparisons are counted separately. Open the suggested faller's history first. Investigation priority is absolute position change multiplied by recorded impressions, not estimated lost clicks. Movement lists show three queries initially and up to five when expanded.

## Dates and coverage

Choose 30, 90, 180, 480 or 1825 days. The last option means the last five years of archive, not all history. Month labels are approximate; data details give exact dates on the America/Los_Angeles calendar. The end assumes a three-day lag, without live completeness verification. Imports request Google's final data only.

Complete API responses, application-limited days, failed days and unknown coverage are counted separately. Existing archive days are not retroactively marked complete. Even a completed response excludes Google's hidden and omitted queries. Last observed date differs from scanned-through date. Continue filling may require several runs. Existing history remains readable during sync.

## Distribution and query work

Distribution covers the full observed current population. Positions are rounded: 3.4 belongs to the first group, 3.5 to the second. Bars are relative to the largest group; the percentage is the share of observed queries. Band changes are net changes across the same comparable queries. No comparison is never displayed as zero.

Search and filters cover the archive beyond the former first hundred. Facet counts respect text and other active filters. High impressions includes ties at the upper-quartile threshold. Top 10 includes queries without a previous observation. Dropped out of top 10 requires observations in both periods. Clear all filters with one button. Pages contain 25, 50 or 100 records; summaries do not depend on page size.

Queries observed previously but absent now have a separate list. Absence does not prove a ranking loss or position zero. This list shows the first 25 by impressions and also follows the search text.

## Reading history

Position means are impression-weighted. Change is previous mean minus current mean. Below 0.05 places is neutral; significant-movement filters use 0.5. Detail uses the same period comparison as the table. The first/last recorded-day pair is separate evidence.

Observed days always remain visible: 10 days in a 90-day period is not complete coverage. Daily points use real calendar spacing and gaps break the line. Arrow keys, Home and End inspect dates. Expand daily values for a readable list. Whole missing weeks remain gaps in weekly lines; edge weeks can be partial.

The Search performance link preserves the exact query and archive dates. For periods older than Google's retention, the earliest readable date is explained before navigation. Competitor rankings, paid search volume and traffic forecasts are unavailable.

When no queries were observed in both periods, rises and falls cannot be calculated. The movement card explains this instead of presenting measured zero movement. Expansion is offered only when more than three movements exist.

---

# Opportunities

URL: https://seowatcher.io/en/docs/opportunities/

> Which page to work on first: pages Google already shows, ranked by an upper bound on extra clicks from your Search Console data, with suggested work.

Opportunities ranks the pages Google already shows for your site by how many extra clicks they could bring. The calculation uses your own Search Console data and your site's own click-through rates. Each page gets a suggested kind of work and an upper bound on the gain; it is not a forecast or a guarantee.

## How to use Opportunities

Start with **Look here first**. It opens the page with the highest estimable additional-click upper bound and suggests work to investigate. It does not measure how easy or fast the work will be.

## Dates and scope

Choose 7, 28 or 90 days. Search Console uses complete days on Google's Pacific calendar. If Google supplies no completeness boundary, the app labels its reporting-lag assumption. Actual start and end dates remain visible. Analytics reads the same calendar dates in its property's timezone, which may cover a different interval of time.

The **upper bound scaled to 30 days** normalizes the selected window. It is not a calendar-month forecast, a guarantee or search volume. It covers only fetched, identifiable queries with sufficient evidence. Hidden-query share is unknown, and row limits are disclosed. The dashboard query estimate uses a different model: do not add the two. The current-click comparison uses all clicks on the candidate pages, including brand clicks.

## Worklist and filters

Work and conversion filters combine with AND. The server filters all candidate pages before showing the first 25, 50 or 100 matches. Global totals do not change with filters or row limits. A page may appear in several work categories; their page counts are not additive. Period, row limit and filters stay in the URL.

Desktop has a sortable table; phones have wrapping page rows and a Details action. Details show impressions, position, target position band and the allocated contribution for each query. The top ten queries are shown with a separate remainder. Allocated queries plus the remainder reconcile with the page's displayed bound. The CTR gap uses only comparable non-brand queries and the same supported impressions on both sides, in percentage points.

## Unknown evidence and Analytics

Unestimable scope does not mean no opportunity. Missing query matches, low impressions and missing target rates are counted separately from measured zero. No returned page rows does not prove there were no impressions.

Analytics adds observed organic sessions, key events and the share of sessions with a key event. It never projects future event counts from additional clicks. Restricted metrics stay unknown. Source limits and timezones are disclosed. URL variants may share one Analytics cohort; do not sum its sessions across rows. For quota errors, wait and refresh; for permission errors, check connection settings. A failed refresh preserves previous evidence with its original dates and a warning.

“Inspect Analytics address group” in a row or its detail opens organic landing pages with the source dates and normalized address group. When the address or dates cannot be matched, an explanation replaces the link. The group is filtered before pagination within the same source of up to 1,000 rows used by Opportunities. Analytics discloses source or quality limits that prevent verification of the complete group. Refetched measurements may change; matching date labels can cover different time spans in the GA4 property timezone and Search Console Pacific calendar.

## Export and follow-up

CSV and Sheets exports include the displayed filtered rows, observed dates, normalized upper-bound unit, model, property, brand source, source limits and Analytics cohort. Sheets writes happen only when you select the export action.

Open in Search performance preserves the source start/end dates and opens the exact URL's detail panel. Unreadable periods are explained instead of substituting other dates. Record your change, then compare measured clicks, CTR and position for equivalent periods. A shrinking estimate alone does not prove success. Low rank or a low estimate does not justify deleting content; consider merging only after confirming overlapping intent.

Thin data does not mean zero potential gain. Missing usable non-brand queries may result from hidden queries, brand exclusions or data limits. The longest period never suggests extending it again. Open Search performance to review queries with impressions. Calculation details expand under Data coverage and calculation.

Pages with impressions and unknown gain also appear: estimated pages first by gain, then unknown pages by impressions. Unknown gain is not zero; totals sum only computed gains. Details list observed non-brand queries by impressions and mark pages with only brand queries. Suggestions use position alone (1–5 review title/snippet, 6–10 content, 11–20 internal links/content, 21+ search intent); they do not prove low CTR or future gain. Work filters match these suggestions; conversion filters use observed Analytics signals. CSV and Sheets leave unknown gain blank and include status, reason, brand marker and observed queries.

When gain is unknown, inspect the page and observed queries first; consider title or content changes only after confirming a mismatch. When all gains are unknown, work categories show candidate counts without gain bars. The conversion summary separates matched pages from pages with unknown conversion status; missing Analytics coverage does not mean zero conversions. A conversion filter button appears only when confirmed records exist. Source and period are labelled facts; calculations remain in the closed disclosure. Missing Analytics data is explained in page details rather than repeated on every row.

---

# Saved keywords

URL: https://seowatcher.io/en/docs/saved-keywords/

> Review saved keywords with dated Search Console observations. Understand archive coverage, missing data and changes within the selected period.

Save important queries from Search performance or Rankings. Saving does not start a new Google tracker: this screen matches your chosen records to observations already stored locally.

## Dates and counts

Choose 30, 90 or 180 days; the default is 90. Exact current and equally long previous dates are shown. Dates use Google's Pacific calendar and an assumed three-day lag, which does not prove archive completeness.

Cards show saved records matching text and tags, observed records, comparable significant movements and unknown rank evidence. Band bars use this same base; selecting one narrows the table. These are records, not all site queries or search volume. Separate saved market records retain their IDs and counts, while archive observations cover all countries and devices.

Position is impression weighted. Matching compacts whitespace and uses Turkish case rules, preserving I/ı versus İ/i. Raw variants are combined by impressions. Missing evidence is never rank zero or a proven loss. Significant movement means at least half a place; a smaller change may still appear in row detail. No comparison differs from unchanged.

## Investigate a record

The table shows the word, average position, change, impressions and tags. On phones, key metrics sit under the word. Open Archive details for the same dates, raw variants, previous mean, observed days and saved market. Creation date and any legacy intent remain in detail; intent is not newly measured. The secondary Search performance link searches containing text over its live last-28-day view, so it is not an exact archive reconciliation.

Every include term must match; none of the exclude terms may match. Each box accepts at most 20 terms. Any selected tag matches, up to 50 selected tags; this is not a limit on tags stored in the project. Tag counts are project-wide assignments. Filters, band, period, sort and page persist in the URL. Clear all also clears an empty active band.

## Repair missing evidence

Disconnected, never imported, partial archive and failed reads have separate explanations. Refresh list only rereads local storage. Use the Rankings archive update action for newer Google observations; connect Search Console first if needed. Google may omit rare queries, so absence from the archive does not prove absence from search.

## Exports and bulk actions

CSV and Sheets use the same filtered population and evidence fields. Existing word, intent, tags and creation columns stay first; appended fields include current/prior position, delta, status, observed days, exact dates, coverage, variants, scope, market, record ID and snapshot. Unknown measurements are blank. If the underlying snapshot changes during export, restart it.

Selection covers this page only. Pending filters or refresh disable actions on stale rows. Removal asks for confirmation; editing a tag does not remove words. Creation time remains the default ordering; position, movement, impressions and word can also be sorted. Inspect declines orders significant paired declines for investigation and does not establish their cause.

**Daily observations.** Request daily history explicitly inside Archive details. It uses the same dates and matching rule, leaves missing days as gaps, supports keyboard date inspection and includes a text list of daily values.

When no saved keywords can be compared, the movement card shows No comparison instead of zero. When all saved keywords were observed, the Position unknown card does not warn about missing observations. Movement and unknown-position card buttons are disabled when they have no matching results.

---

# Understanding Analytics data

URL: https://seowatcher.io/en/docs/analytics/

> Analytics shows measured visits, engagement and key events from your GA4 property.

Analytics shows measured visits, engagement and key events from your GA4 property. The report selector offers landing pages, pages, acquisition, key events, ecommerce, site search, audience and measurement health.

## Read the scope first

Unknown measurements are shown as **Could not determine traffic for this period**, with known values preserved. Reported restrictions appear beside the metrics; an unknown cause is stated explicitly. Retry or inspect measurement settings; changing the channel is not suggested as a repair for unreadable data. Background notes are collapsed under **Understanding Analytics data**; scope, dates and warnings remain visible.

Organic search includes search engines beyond Google. All traffic changes both the overview and report. Site search always covers measured search-result events from all traffic and has no channel toggle. All hosts and streams in the property are included. Another site or app can contribute to these totals.

The 7, 28 and 90-day windows end yesterday in the property time zone. Yesterday is an elapsed calendar day, not a guarantee that data is final. Recent days may be reprocessed. Current and previous equal-length dates and the time zone are shown. Links accept paired startDate/endDate values; future end dates are clamped to yesterday with a notice. GA4 and Search Console use different calendars and measures. Matching date labels do not guarantee matching time spans.

## Inspect outcomes and rows

Opportunities links open the same normalized address group and source dates using `pageGroup`. This server filter reads every organic landing-page row from Google, page by page, before the 50/100/200-row screen pagination. Query strings and trailing slashes share a group; different hosts and case-sensitive paths remain separate. A source cap or quality restriction is disclosed as an unverified complete group; an empty result does not prove no traffic. The overview retains its property scope. You can remove the group filter; the URL, Back navigation and exports preserve the group scope.

The overview follows the selected scope: sessions, engagement rate, key events and purchase revenue. Key events are not unique customers. Zero revenue does not prove there is no shop. Unknown currency is named beside the amount. Engagement duration is total time, not the average per user. Daily values distinguish unknown days from zero. Quality restrictions qualify the data and suppress confident comparisons or advice.

Choose 50, 100 or 200 rows per page and use Previous/Next to reach later rows. Filters, sorting, summaries and exports cover the listed page only. Selecting a bar filters the table without changing the summary base. Users can recur across categories: never sum them into unique property users. Equal paths on different hosts and equal item names with different IDs remain distinct. Revenue share charts are withheld for negative or unknown values.

The low-conversion filter is an investigation heuristic over at least four eligible listed pages with at least 30 sessions each. It does not estimate lost sales. No observed key events does not prove missing configuration; check measurement health. Popular internal searches do not prove missing content.

## Share, verify and check quota

Report, channel, dates, breakdown, page size and offset persist in the URL. Exact host/path filtering covers listed rows only and does not combine URL variants. CSV and Sheets export the filtered rows with raw numeric cells. The ga4_scope_json column preserves provider, property, dates, time zone, currency, quality, page and filters.

Measurement health reads Admin settings only. “No gaps found in the settings checked” does not prove the tag sends data; follow the linked collection checks. Partial inventory counts say at least. When enhanced measurement is off, zero child features are effectively on. No account settings are changed.

The collapsed quota section shows a local snapshot from the latest report response, not traffic-period usage. The standard property ceiling is an assumption. Refresh requests the visible reports again and can spend reporting tokens.

When Google truncates data in the requested date range, the Analytics overview and report details show the reason and dates supplied by Google. The report is treated as limited; incomplete coverage is not presented as a reliable period comparison.

---

# Site audit

URL: https://seowatcher.io/en/docs/site-audit/

> Audit your site against 202 rules and review issues by priority. Understand the audit score, measurement coverage and incomplete results.

This screen finds the problems on your site and tells you how to fix them.

The app walks through your site with its own crawler (a program that opens and reads pages one by one). It looks for broken links, missing titles and slow pages. At the end you get a score and a list of problems ranked by importance, each with instructions for fixing it. The score also shows how many of the checks could be measured. An audit that stopped halfway gets no score.

## What is on the screen

**Start a new audit card.** It has these fields.

- **Address of the site to crawl**: your project's domain is filled in already.
- **Crawl up to N pages**: at least 10, at most 10,000, default 50. If you enter more than 500, the app asks you to confirm.
- **Also measure page speed**: off by default. If you turn it on, every page is measured on a phone and on a computer. Google Lighthouse (Google's page measuring tool) does the measuring. The card tells you in advance the least time it will take.
- **Also check outgoing links and image sizes**: after the crawl, it checks whether links to other sites open and how big your image files are. At most 300 addresses are asked about. Sites that block bots are skipped.

If you have no PageSpeed key (the free code Google gives for speed measurement), speed measurement is limited to 50 pages. To measure all pages, add a free key in **Settings**. **Start audit** starts the audit. The **Quotas** section below it is closed. Open it to see the current state of the PageSpeed and URL inspection quotas.

**Previous audits.** Each audit is listed with its date, address, status, page count and problem counts. The Critical, Warning and Info columns show all stored findings, including page findings and site-wide checks; one page may have multiple findings. If more than one site has been audited in the project, a site picker appears above the list. Density means issues per hundred pages. Trend lines and change arrows appear only when stored evidence confirms the same site, page population, crawl settings and measured checks. Different or unknown scopes are shown as independent counts; change cannot be determined. While several sites are selected, the chart is hidden. **View** on a row opens the audit. The row menu has **Run again with the same settings** and **Delete audit**. Deleting also deletes the audit's pages, problems and speed measurements, and cannot be undone.

**Audit details.** At the top, **Download report** downloads a one-file HTML report and saves it in **Reports**. Below it, yellow warnings appear when needed (see below). Then comes the score card.

**Score card.** It shows these things.

- In the middle, the **Site score** and a rating word beside it: **Excellent**, **Good**, **Average** or **Poor**.
- Below it, a coverage line: "Score based on the 142 checks that were measured. 38 checks could not be measured." The question mark beside it explains how the score is worked out.
- A one-sentence verdict. If the score is held at a limit, it says why.
- **URLs found: N, crawled: M**. How many addresses the crawl found on the site and how many it opened. If the audit stopped at the page limit you chose, a note says "The audit was limited to N pages; the site may have more pages." The score still stands in that case.
- Lines for heavy categories that could not be measured. For example "Speed not measured: the PageSpeed quota ran out".
- Four counters: **Critical issues**, **Improvements** (warnings and info), **Checks passed** and **Not measured**.
- **Category scores**: Crawling, Content, Indexing, Speed, Security, Accessibility, Social and structured data. The lowest is at the top. If you click a category, the **Checks** tab opens on that category. A category nothing could be measured in says "Not measured". One that was partly measured says "Partial data".
- **Score history**: the scores of the latest audits of the same site. It appears once two audits have a score. Grey bars are partial scores. Audits that got no score are not on the chart, and a line below says how many there are.

**Tabs.**

- **To-do (N)**: the jobs, starting with the one that adds the most points. Each job shows the points you would gain, a "Small task", "Medium task" or "Large task" label and a **How to fix it** box. If Search Console is connected, the order also takes the clicks of the affected pages into account.
- **Checks (N)**: every check, by category. Each shows as passed, failed or not measured. For those not measured, the reason is written.
- **Instant data**: the site beyond its pages. Things like the certificate, the domain registration, DNS and a preview of the site.
- **Pages with issues (N)**: groups the problems. Open a card to see the cause, the affected addresses and the **How to fix it** box. You can search the addresses.
- **Pages (N)**: every page that was crawled. Quick filters: **Blocked from indexing**, **Slow** (more than 1 second), **Missing alt text**, **Not in sitemap**.
- **Index status**: Google's answer for each page. It is covered in its own guide. If the audited site does not belong to the project's Search Console property, this tab does not show Google data and the screen explains why.
- **Speed (N)**: appears only if speed measurement was on. If some pages could not be measured, the number is written like "10/12".

The **Export** menu at the top right gives the list on the open tab as **Export to Sheets**, **CSV** or **JSON**. If a filter is on, only the visible rows go.

## The three states of the score

**Full score.** When most of the checks were measured, it comes with a rating word. Read the score by these ranges: 90 and above is Excellent, 70 and above Good, 50 and above Average, below that Poor.

**Partial score.** If the share of measured checks falls below 70 percent, the score is partial. It is also partial if fewer than half the checks in Crawling, Indexing, Content or Speed were measured. The card reads "Partial score, measurement coverage 62%", gives no rating word and is in a neutral colour. The number reflects only the checks that could be seen. No judgement, good or bad, was made about the rest. The usual reasons are these: the PageSpeed quota ran out, there is no PageSpeed key, speed measurement was off, or no index data could be fetched from Search Console.

**No score given.** In these cases the card says "Incomplete audit, no score given" in place of the score.

- The audit stopped with an error.
- The audit is still running.
- The crawl stopped early because of the site's rate limit. The issue list is incomplete, so a score would only be a guess.
- No page could be crawled. In that case the score card does not appear at all.

The findings are still shown and apply to the pages that were crawled. Run the audit again for a full score.

## If the audit stopped, what it says

When an audit fails, the screen tells you three things: what happened, whether the fault is in your site or in the app, and what to do. The title says in which phase it stopped: **URL discovery**, **crawl**, **speed test** or **results preparation**.

| What the screen says                                                                 | Whose side              | What to do                                                                        |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ----------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| A step did not finish in time                                                        | Most likely your site   | Try again in a few minutes. If it happens again, start with fewer pages           |
| The audit did not fit in the memory the app can use                                  | The app                 | Start again with fewer pages                                                      |
| The audit went over the processor time the app allows                                | The app                 | Start again with fewer pages                                                      |
| An error occurred while writing the results to the database                          | The app                 | Check that the disk has free space, restart the app and start the audit again     |
| The result of one step was larger than the app can store                             | The app                 | Start again with fewer pages                                                      |
| The app's internal audit engine reported an error                                    | The app                 | Choose **Yeniden başlat** (Restart) in the tray menu, then start the audit again  |
| The audit was cut off                                                                | The app                 | Make sure the app stays open and start the audit again                            |
| The install key did not reach the part that runs audits (your keys were not deleted) | The app                 | Update or restart the app, then start the audit again                             |
| The audit stopped with an unexpected error                                           | Could not be determined | Start again. If it keeps happening, download the diagnostics bundle from **Help** |

The raw error text does not reach the screen. It stays in the diagnostics bundle.

## Yellow warnings during the crawl

- **The audit could not fully crawl this site.** The site's bot protection stopped the crawler. The results are still shown. Allow "seotracker-audit" in your firewall, or try one of the desktop crawlers the guide suggests.
- **N pages could not be fetched (network error).** The connection could not be made even on a retry. These pages were not audited and are not counted as broken. It is often temporary. Run the audit again. If it continues, check that the site opens from this computer.
- **The site rate-limited N pages.** The site said "too many requests". Those pages could not be audited. Start again after the rate limit resets.
- **The crawl stopped early because of the site's rate limit.** The wait that was asked for was longer than the audit may take. The report is incomplete and gets no score.
- **The saved PageSpeed key could not be read, so the speed test ran without a key.** The audit finished, but the speed test ran without a key. The crawl results are not affected. The speed test was limited to the first pages only. Update or restart the app, then start a new audit. If it continues, save the PageSpeed key again in **Settings**.

## How to use it

1. For the first audit, leave the page count at 50. Keep speed measurement off. It finishes in a minute or two. With speed measurement off the score can come out partial. That is normal.
2. Read the coverage line on the score card. If it says **Partial score**, the lines below it tell you why.
3. Start with the first three jobs in the **To-do** tab. They give the most points for the least effort.
4. In the **Pages with issues** tab, finish the critical problems first. A critical problem stops Google from seeing the page.
5. Take the list with **Export** and give it to your site administrator. You can pass the **How to fix it** box on as it is.
6. After fixing, click **Run again with the same settings**. The arrows in the **Previous audits** list and the **Score history** show what was fixed.
7. Turn on speed measurement once a week, for important pages. Each page takes about ten seconds and uses Google quota.

## How the numbers are calculated

**Score.** Each finding takes points off its own category. How much depends on how important the finding is and what share of pages it touches. The weights are: critical 40, warning 15, info 3. The site score is the weighted average of seven categories. Crawling and Indexing weigh the most, Social and structured data the least. A check that could not be measured neither raises nor lowers the score. That is why coverage is shown separately.

**Upper limits.** If there is even one problem, the score is at most 99. If there is a critical problem, it is at most 69. With 5 or more warnings it is at most 89. This way, one page blocked from indexing on a big site is not hidden under a high score. If a limit holds the score, the card says so. The "+N points" beside a job takes the limit into account too. Fixing the only critical problem lifts the whole limit. Fixing one warning while a limit is on adds very little.

**Crawl.** The app does not strain your site. It sends at most two requests at a time. If the site says "too many requests" (429), it waits. If the total wait goes over 30 minutes, the crawl stops and the audit gets no score.

**Speed measurement.** On a site of 212 pages, the whole audit took 35 minutes. About 24 of them were speed measurement. If the daily quota runs out, measuring stops, the results so far stay and the score may be partial. A problem is written in these cases:

- The main content shows later than 4 seconds (LCP).
- The content shifts more than 0.25 (CLS).
- The response to a click takes longer than 500 milliseconds (INP).
- The Lighthouse SEO score is below 90.

## Frequently asked
