**Does the audit show what Google sees?** No. The app's crawler reads the page itself. Google's answer is in the **Index status** tab.

**The score is 98, why not 100?** Even one problem keeps the score at 99 or less.

**Why is my score stuck at 69?** There is a critical problem. The score cannot go past 69 until you fix it. The card says so.

**Why does it say "Partial score"?** A large share of the checks could not be measured. The coverage line and the lines below it tell you why. Turning on speed measurement or connecting Search Console usually raises coverage.

**Why does it say "Incomplete audit" instead of a score?** The audit stopped halfway or early. The issue list is incomplete, so no score is given. Run the audit again.

**What does the "blocked" warning mean?** Your site's bot protection stopped the crawler. Allow "seotracker-audit" in your firewall.

**Speed measurement stopped halfway.** Usually there is no PageSpeed key, or the daily quota is used up. The quota card in **Settings** says which.

**How many audits run at once?** At most three. Two audits measuring speed slow each other down.

## Limits

The crawler may not see content that JavaScript (code that runs on the page) adds later. An audit crawls at most 10,000 pages. Speed measurement is Google's lab measurement, not real visitor data. The audit changes nothing on your site. You or your assistant make the fixes.

In Previous audits, **Pages crawled** is the number of addresses actually crawled, including failed audits; it is not the initial page limit. Critical and warning columns show total findings. **Speed measurement requested** means the audit was started with speed measurement enabled; it does not prove the measurement finished successfully. On a phone, scroll the table sideways for the other columns and actions.



History lists critical, warning and informational page findings; one page may have several findings. Completed jobs show the recorded crawl limit, or explicitly say it was not recorded. Scope details opens measured and unmeasured checks. Failed runs show the stored failure explanation and next step; an unknown cause is stated explicitly.

---

# Index status

URL: https://seowatcher.io/en/docs/index-status/

> Google's answer for each of your pages: is it in search, if not why, and when it last visited. You can ask at most 2,000 queries a day.

This tab shows which of your pages Google has put into search.

The site audit tells you a page can be opened, but not whether Google has added it to its index (Google's list of pages). The **Index status** tab asks Google and saves the answer on this computer. A page is asked about again only when its answer has gone stale. This matters because Google allows 2,000 questions a day per property (your site's record in Search Console), and the app and your assistant share that allowance.

## What is on the screen

**The "What has Google done with these pages?" chart.** This donut chart splits the crawled pages into three groups:

- **On Google**: can appear in search.
- **Not indexed**: Google looked at the page but did not add it.
- **Awaiting an answer**: not asked yet, or no answer could be received.

**Summary boxes.** They show how many pages were asked about, how many are in the index, how many are not and how many are waiting. The "Pages where Google chose a different canonical" box counts pages where Google chose a different address from the canonical you declared (the tag that names a page's main address). The "Not yet checked in this audit" box shows how many pages are left to ask about.

**The "Check status on Google" button.** Each press asks about at most 25 pages, starting with those that have gone longest without an answer. When the daily limit is used up, the warning "Google's daily limit of 2,000 URLs is used up" appears, with the number of pages still waiting. The button is disabled if Search Console is not connected or if the audited domain is outside the connected property.

**Table.** Columns: **Page**, **Status**, **Reason**, **Google-selected canonical**, **Google's last crawl**. The status cell shows "Google'da", "Not checked", "No answer", "Error", or the Turkish version of Google's own status. The app translates 18 statuses into Turkish. Examples:

- "Discovered - currently not indexed"
- "Excluded by 'noindex' tag" (the page is kept out of search)
- "Blocked by robots.txt" (robots.txt is the file that tells Google which pages it may visit)
- "Soft 404" (the page exists but Google treats it as empty)
- "URL is unknown to Google"

You can download the table as CSV.

## How to use it

1. When the audit finishes, open the tab. If the "Awaiting an answer" number is high, press **Check status on Google**. Each press covers 25 more pages, so a few presses are enough for a small site.
2. Look at the "Not indexed" group first. The **Reason** column gives Google's reason, which often tells you what to do. If it says "Blocked by robots.txt", remove the block. If it says "Excluded by 'noindex' tag", remove the tag. If it says "Discovered - currently not indexed", waiting is usually enough.
3. Add important pages that say "Google bu adresi bilmiyor" to your sitemap and submit the sitemap to Search Console. For the three or four most important pages, also click "Dizine eklenmesini iste" (Request indexing) by hand in Search Console.
4. If the "Pages where Google chose a different canonical" box is not zero, look at the **Google-selected canonical** column. Google disagrees with the main address you declared. Either correct yours or make the address Google chose the main one.
5. Press again after a few days. Only stale answers are asked again, so your quota is not wasted.

## How the numbers are calculated

If Google says "indexed", the page counts as "On Google". If it says "not indexed" or "unknown", the page counts as "Not indexed". If there is no answer, the page is "Awaiting an answer".

An answer is treated as stale after a set time and is asked about again: 14 days for a page in the index, 3 days for a page not in the index or an answer with an error. A page that has never been asked about is always eligible. The daily limit is calculated from the number of questions in the last 24 hours. The app counts only its own questions; queries you run by hand in Search Console are not in this counter, but they do count against Google's real limit.

A canonical mismatch means the address Google chose differs from the one you declared, even by a trailing slash.

If Google's last crawl is older than 90 days, the audit reports the problem "Google hasn't crawled this page in a long time". Stale answers are collected into a single problem, "Google's answers for some pages are out of date".

## Frequently asked questions

**Why is the button disabled?** There are three possible reasons: Search Console is not connected, there are no pages left to ask about, or the audited domain is outside the connected property (for example, because you audited another site).

**What does the 2,000 limit apply to?** The property. Two projects connected to the same property, and your assistant, spend from the same pool.

**What should I do for a page that says "Discovered - currently not indexed"?** Usually nothing. On new sites Google can leave pages waiting for weeks. Linking to the page from pages that Google crawls often speeds it up.

**Does this tab tell Google about new pages?** No, it only asks. To tell Google about a page, use the sitemap and "Dizine eklenmesini iste" in Search Console.

## Limits

The answers are only as good as what Google returns, and Google can leave some fields empty. You cannot go over 2,000 questions a day, so covering a 10,000-page site takes five days. The tab asks only about crawled pages; addresses that were not part of the audit do not appear in the list.

---

# Reports and templates

URL: https://seowatcher.io/en/docs/reports/

> Save audit, search performance and assistant reports as standalone HTML files. Open them on a phone, print them or share them by email.

Reports are saved HTML documents for this project. Opening one does not refresh Google data. The save time is not the observation date of its sources.

## Create a report

**Prepare Search report** opens Search performance. Select the period, device, country and search type, then download its report. **Prepare audit report** opens Site audit; select the crawl there. Copy the report command to ask your assistant to write a report. Templates are instructions for the assistant, not native generators or schedules. Reports are saved before downloading. If downloading fails, retry from this library. Saved documents remain readable when a source disconnects.

## Read and search the library

The latest updated report appears first with its saved summary, save time and open/download actions. Missing summaries and unrecorded structured periods are stated explicitly: inspect the document for its source dates and limitations. Neither the title nor HTML is mined to invent provenance.

Search covers titles and saved summaries. Type counts use the search and recent filters before the selected type. Recent means distinct files saved or updated during the rolling seven days, not edit events or fresh Google observations. Matching results and the full project inventory are separate counts.

The server returns 25 metadata rows per page. Reports beyond the first 100 remain searchable and reachable with Previous/Next. Updated time is the default order, so editing an old file raises it. Creation-time and title ordering are available. Search, type, recent, sort and page stay in the URL for Back and reload.

Legacy native Search and Audit reports share a creator marker. They read **App report, type not recorded**, rather than all being counted as audits. Recorded assistant skills and template names remain visible. File count is not SEO progress. Size means stored HTML bytes; download security metadata can make the downloaded file slightly larger.

## Open, download and print

The document opens inside an opaque frame without script or network permissions. Expand Source and save details for attribution, type, bytes and timestamps. The saved language remains fixed. Deliberately regenerate from the source screen for another language or current measurements.

Download HTML for offline reading or sending to another person. Print to PDF opens a browser tab; if blocked, allow popups or open the report in a new tab and print there. Fullscreen isolates background keyboard focus and keeps exit buttons above and below the document. A copied app link belongs to this installation; share the file itself.

A preview that has not opened after 15 seconds offers Retry and Open in new tab. Missing documents, access, connection and download-server problems have recovery messages. Failed list refreshes preserve cached rows with a warning. An unavailable storage check does not prove free capacity.

## Search report evidence

The cover shows the actual resolved dates, previous period, filters and generation time. Search days use Pacific time. When Google supplies no finality boundary, the report says the last days were excluded using a lag assumption. A truncated residual query share includes privacy-hidden queries and rows beyond the cap. Query, page and query-by-page caps can limit opportunities; their row sums are not site totals.

Overlap analysis prints its own period and thresholds even with zero results. A seven-day report can use a 28-day overlap window. Multiple pages appearing for a query do not prove lost clicks or SEO harm. Unavailable long-history or appearance data is not a zero. Capped lists state shown and observed counts. The request budget belongs to the Search view and excludes additional overlap analysis and cache effects.

Generation re-reads server data. Google can revise past measurements and the period may be resolved again, so exact equality with an earlier screen is not guaranteed. The same localized title can be replaced; changing language may create another document. Long titles fit storage and include a server-derived collision guard for source/filter combinations.

## Templates and storage

Template limits: 80 characters for name, 200 for description, 3,000 for instructions, ten templates per project. Deleting a template preserves its reports. Clear search restores hidden templates.

Storage guards are 500,000 bytes per report, 120 title characters, 2,500 summary characters, 10,000 reports per project and 5 GB across the installation. These guard storage, not SEO coverage. For Audit reports inspect the document's own method for crawl, speed and optional Google evidence dates.

## Source kinds and regeneration

New native Search performance and Site audit reports have separate saved kinds. Older app reports are not classified from their titles. Search identity uses the property, resolved dates and filters; Audit identity uses the audit ID. Regenerating the same source in another language updates the same record and may change its language. Title collisions with agent reports are refused; an older document with the same title is preserved and the new save is refused.

Regenerate native reports from their source screen; agents cannot replace their content using `save_report`. Missing source data is never treated as zero. Audit methodology identifies the GSC traffic period, source row limit and available stored mobile CrUX measurement.

The saved report at the top is not a current summary of the site. The source site is shown when the original audit verifies it; a different project site triggers a warning. Without verified provenance, the report may concern another site. Legacy reports are labelled with an unverified source and date. **Open site audits** opens the audit history. If a suitable saved audit exists, open it and download its report; this link does not start an audit or create a report automatically. Historical files remain unchanged.

---

# Project context

URL: https://seowatcher.io/en/docs/project-context/

> Project context stores local notes that you and a connected assistant can use. Filled text is not verified, and not every assistant necessarily reads it.

Project context stores local notes that you and a connected assistant can use. Filled text is not verified, and not every assistant necessarily reads it.

## Start with the goal

The lead shows filled main sections and the stored goal. Open the first empty section or use **Go to section**. Business overview, current goal, positioning and writing preferences each allow 4,000 characters. Each section shows its last author and absolute update time. **Save changes** saves changed main sections only.

Competitors and key pages are optional curated lists, not ranking or conversion measurements. Each allows 100 entries. Competitor domain/name/notes limits are 255/120/500 characters. Page URL/topic/notes limits are 2,048/200/500. Roles are your labels. Assistants create custom sections; you can edit or remove them. Limits: 20 custom sections, 120 characters per title and 4,000 per body.

## Save and refresh

Refresh reads notes and setup again. A failed background read retains stored information and drafts with a warning. Leaving with unsaved main or inline changes triggers a warning. The server does not yet prevent simultaneous edits of the same section from overwriting each other; compare the latest text before saving when editing with an assistant.

Under **Prepare a draft with an agent**, the prompt asks the assistant to request approval before saving. The application tools can write immediately without another approval gate. The prompt is unavailable until project identity is resolved.

**Research log** shows the newest 20 entries from the last 90 days. Dates use the server's UTC day; entries allow 1,000 characters. Expired entries are filtered on every read, even without new writes. A notice identifies additional entries in this window. This is not a complete history.

If another client changes a section while you edit, the whole save is rejected and your draft is preserved. Compare the original text, latest saved text and your draft, merge them and save again. Agents can send `expectedContent` for the same protection; older clients that omit it remain compatible.

**Sources and setup** counts six shared configuration signals. Missing and unreadable states are separate; optional lists are excluded. A stored connection is not a live data test, a PageSpeed key does not guarantee quota, and an installation-level tool call does not prove this project was read. This is not an SEO score.

# Settings

URL: https://seowatcher.io/en/docs/settings/

> Browser, installation and project scopes; Google credentials, local counters and version checks.

Settings holds the choices that apply to this browser (appearance and language) and to the whole installation (Google credentials, PageSpeed key, limits and updates). A project's name, domain and Google properties live in **Project settings**. This page explains the scope of each setting and where to change it.

## Scope and controls

Appearance is stored in this browser. Choose a language and select **Apply language**; arrow navigation alone does not reload the page. Project market language is a separate setting.

Google credentials apply to all projects in this installation. A service account takes priority. Stored credentials and a selected property do not prove data access. A failed refresh keeps the last configuration visible with a retry action. Select the service account JSON file or use the masked paste field, then save. The private key is never displayed.

Manage project name, domain and property in Project settings. Changing the domain preserves the Google binding and history. Country and language are saved-keyword defaults; choose the country filter separately in Search performance.

## Windows, speed and limits

Windows preferences come from the tray application. Docker shows an informational state without toggles. An unavailable launcher means unknown, not off. Retry reads confirmed values; administrator locks explain why editing is unavailable.

Without a PageSpeed key, the application attempts at most 50 pages per audit. Google can stop requests earlier; a key does not guarantee success. The key test makes one mobile request for example.com, outside the audit measurement counter. It shows a test date; changing the key removes the previous result.

Choose the project in Limits. URL Inspection counts this application's property attempts over a rolling 24 hours. PageSpeed counts audits started in the last 24 hours. GA4 remaining tokens belong to the last response timestamp; the standard-property ceiling is an assumption. Old or missing evidence is unknown. Audit pages come from the latest completed audit for the project domain. Reports and templates count the project's full inventory.

## Updates

In-app version checking contacts GitHub at most every six hours. The Windows tray can check daily independently; Windows settings control automatic installation. Last successful check dates qualify cached version information. Wait and retry for rate/access restrictions; use Help diagnostics for a missing source. An unreadable preference cannot be changed.

## Windows notifications

Right-click the seowatcher tray icon and use **Windows bildirimleri** (Windows notifications, on by default). While the launcher runs, completed/failed audits from all projects and new announcements appear as Windows balloons within about 90 seconds, even with the browser closed or in the background. Click to open the relevant page; several events form one summary. First use skips old events; restarting does not replay seen events. Events received while muted are not replayed later. New-version notifications follow the existing update setting. Windows Focus/Do not disturb can hide notifications. No notifications appear when the launcher is closed. This feature is unavailable in Docker.

# Help

URL: https://seowatcher.io/en/docs/help/

> The setup status card, quick actions, common problems and the diagnostics package you send when you report a problem.

This is the first place to look when something goes wrong. The screen checks your setup, tells you what is missing and takes you to the right setting.

The app's interface comes in six languages: Turkish, English, German, French, Italian and Portuguese. This guide uses the English names; to switch, go to **Settings → Appearance → Language**.

## What is on the screen

**Quick actions**. The buttons at the top:

- **Check status again**: refreshes the card below.
- **Download diagnostics bundle**: downloads the file you send when you report a problem. It contains no secret values.
- **Open the guide**: opens the guide on seowatcher.io.
- **seowatcher.io**: opens the app's website, where the download page and the guide live.
- **Release notes**: opens the dedicated Release notes screen (`/release-notes`).
- **Agent setup**: goes to the assistant connection screen.

**App health.** This card checks this installation’s access, Google connection settings, PageSpeed key, runtime and database. A successful setup check does not prove that your site is healthy or that Google data is current. Unread settings are not treated as successful checks. Read the warning and use **Check status again**. The version and last-check time identify the result. **Copy summary** copies this status as text. Manage project connections with **Open connections**.

**Port number warning.** If the Windows package opens on another port because a different program holds 3001 (for example an old Docker copy using 3001), a yellow strip appears at the top of every screen in the app: "seowatcher is running on 3002 this time because another program is using 3001 (for example an old Docker copy). Google sign-in is set up for 3001; close that program and restart seowatcher." The strip is there in case you missed the notification in the taskbar. Google sign-in goes back to address 3001 and fails if you opened the app on 3002. The close button on the right of the strip hides it for this tab. The same sentence is also written in the **App health** card. To fix it, close the program that holds 3001, then choose **Yeniden başlat** (Restart) in the tray menu. The app goes back to 3001 and the strip disappears. If no other program is using it, the app goes back to 3001 on the next start anyway.

**Projects**. The status of each project's Search Console and Analytics connection. The **Open connections** button takes you to the project settings.

**Common problems**. Six collapsible items: the page won't open or the app isn't running, the port is in use, my agent can't connect (401), speed measurement stops partway (429), no query data, and I changed a setting and the app doesn't see it. Each gives what to do and a link to the matching setting.

**Google and system limits**. With **Show limits** you see the current state of Google's daily limits.

**Bottom list.** Shortcuts to the log files and to the health address (`/api/health`). In the Windows package, logs open with **Open logs** in the taskbar menu. In Docker, use the command given by **Copy command**.

## How to use it

1. If something does not work, open this screen first and read the warning on the card.
2. Press the button next to the warning. It takes you to the right setting. Make the change, come back and click **Check status again**.
3. If setup checks pass but the problem continues, check **Common problems** and the relevant project screen.
4. If it is still not solved, click **Download diagnostics bundle** and attach the file to the issue on GitHub. In the Windows package, **Sorunu bildir (GitHub)** (Report a problem (GitHub)) in the taskbar menu does the same in one click.

## Frequently asked questions

**Why is the "Google sign-in" row yellow?** No Google access key has been entered yet. The row stays yellow until Google is connected. Follow the guide for connecting to Google.

**The "Sign-in and access" row says it is a single-user setup without a password.** This is expected. The app opens only from your own computer. To open it to the outside, put your own password-protected sign-in in front of it.

**What is in the diagnostics package?** The version, setup checks, table counts and phase and error summaries for the latest 25 audits. PageSpeed errors are summarized without page URLs. Secrets and passwords are excluded; project names, domains and Google property IDs may be included. Review the files before sending them.

## Limits

The screen checks only the setup itself. To find a problem on your site, use Site denetimi (Site audit). To see a problem on Google's side, use the Dizin durumu (Index status) screen.

## Which screen should I use?

[Dashboard](https://seowatcher.io/en/docs/dashboard/) summarizes the selected project’s setup and data. [Opportunities](https://seowatcher.io/en/docs/opportunities/) helps you choose work from Search Console data. [Rank tracking](https://seowatcher.io/en/docs/rank-tracking/) follows saved keywords’ average positions in Google data; it is not a live search result. If data is missing, check project connections, the date range and the coverage warning on that screen. Help’s setup result does not validate those reports.

On sites with little search traffic, Google hides some queries. The query list can be empty or show fewer clicks than the page totals; this alone does not mean the connection is broken.
